title: Time bound for buffered sequential composition
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x,y,o$ be Boolean words with $t_1,t_2\in\mathbb{N}$. If $M_1$ computes $y$ from $x$ in exactly $t_1$ steps and $M_2$ computes $o$ from $y$ in exactly $t_2$ steps, then their buffered sequential composition computes $o$ from $x$ in exactly $t_1+|y|+2+t_2$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1,M_2$ are finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
replaced:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be multi-tape Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet,
let $x$, $y$, $o$ be Boolean words, and let $t_1, t_2 \in \mathbb{N}$.
Consider the buffered sequential composition machine of $M_1$ and $M_2$, which
simulates $M_1$ on its input with $M_1$'s output diverted to a buffer work
tape, rewinds the buffer, and then simulates $M_2$ reading the buffer as its
input.  If $M_1$ halts on input $x$ within $t_1$ steps with output $y$, and
$M_2$ halts on input $y$ within $t_2$ steps with output $o$, then this
composition machine halts on input $x$ within $t_1 + \abs{y} + 2 + t_2$ steps
with output $o$.  Neither machine is required to halt on any other input.
